title: Finite Hom scalar/site square and constructible descent
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and integers $n\ge m\ge1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^n)$, $B=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^m)$ with the quotient map [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small etale and pro-etale sites use constant ring sheaves, ordinary uncompleted derived tensor, and derived internal Hom $H_{\tau,R}$ for $\tau=\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet}$, $R=A,B$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Write $D^b_{ctf}$ for bounded constructible cohomology of finite Tor amplitude, tested against every degree-zero module sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-kun-tor-amplitude, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Let $U_R=\nu_X^*$ for $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proet}}\to X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and let $F_{\tau}=-\otimes_A^LB$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. For each scalar or site pullback, use its canonical ringed tensor comparison.

Every $P\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{proet}},R)$ admits $P'\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},R)$ and an isomorphism $U_RP'\cong P$; any bounded constructible etale witness for $P$ has the same Tor interval as $P$. The exact $U_R$ preserve these categories and their Tor intervals. There is a natural $B$-linear isomorphism
$$h_T:U_BF_{\mathrm{et}}T\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\mathrm{proet}}U_AT,$$
which on flat-term K-flat models is induced by the ordinary constant-coefficient tensor identification. It is monoidal, including its unit, associativity and symmetry compatibilities, and coherent for $A\to B\to C$, $C=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^r)$, $1\le r\le m$, under successive scalar-extension associators.

For $K,M\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and for their reductions over $B$, the canonical evaluation comparisons $\beta_R:U_RH_{\mathrm{et},R}\to H_{\mathrm{proet},R}(U_R-,U_R-)$ are isomorphisms. Let $v_{\tau}$ be the transpose of reduced evaluation on site $\tau$. Then, as maps $U_BF_{\mathrm{et}}H_{\mathrm{et},A}(K,M)\to H_{\mathrm{proet},B}(F_{\mathrm{proet}}U_AK,F_{\mathrm{proet}}U_AM)$, one has the equality
$$v_{\mathrm{proet}}\circ F_{\mathrm{proet}}(\beta_A)\circ h_{H_{\mathrm{et},A}(K,M)}=H_{\mathrm{proet},B}(h_K^{-1},h_M)\circ\beta_B\circ U_B(v_{\mathrm{et}}).$$
This square carries naturality, evaluation, preservation of tensor–Hom transposes, internal-Hom composition, identity and successive-quotient equations from the etale comparisons to the pro-etale comparisons on every finite-Tor constructible pair. No invertibility of $v_{\mathrm{et}}$ or $v_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is assumed or concluded here.
